**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Stems at/near the soil line
- **Key features**:
  - Bleached white to gray stem lesions at the base
  - Visible fluffy white cottony growth on the stems
  - Dark bodies (sclerotia) embedded within the white mold on the stem surface
  - Dried, dead stem tissue with characteristic white bleached appearance
  - Stem girdling visible at the node area

**Reasoning:**

The image shows soybean stems at ground level with the hallmark signs of White Mold (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*): fluffy white mycelial growth on stems, bleached/whitened stem lesions, and hard black sclerotia embedded within the white mold. The stems are dry and bleached white — exactly as described in the White Mold symptom profile. No other class matches this combination of white cottony growth + black sclerotia on stems.
